Spawning Potential Ratio Calculations in rFAMS

2026-11-13

Source: vignettes/articles/spr.qmd

Overview

Spawning Potential Ratio (SPR) is the proportion of reproductive output produced by an exploited population relative to the reproductive output expected from an unfished population (Goodyear 1993). SPR provides a biological measure of the effect of fishing mortality on the reproductive capacity of a stock and is commonly used as a biological reference point in fisheries management. Once a target SPR benchmark has been selected, managers can estimate the fishing mortality rate required to achieve that benchmark. Target SPR values are often species-specific; however, a threshold of SPR = 0.40 (40%) has been adopted for several groundfish stocks in the northeastern United States (NEFSC 2008). Because SPR is directly related to the reproductive capacity of a population, it is commonly used to evaluate the risk of recruitment overfishing. Management measures such as minimum length limits, slot length limits, and harvest restrictions can be used to achieve desired SPR benchmarks by protecting sexually mature individuals and preserving spawning output.

Although SPR has historically been used extensively in marine fisheries management (Cooper et al. 2013; Goethel et al. 2018; Mu et al. 2021; Willems et al. 2023; Guo et al. 2025), applications in freshwater fisheries have become increasingly common. For example, LaBrie et al. (2025) used SPR to develop harvest commendations for Blue Sucker Cycleptus elongatus, a species not traditionally managed as a sport fish. Similarly, Slipke, et al. (2002) proposed a target SPR of 10-20% for Channel Catfish Ictalurus punctatus for the Upper Mississippi River commercial fishery. Kern et al. (2020) estimated SPR for Shoal Bass Micropterus cataractae and concluded that the population was experiencing recruitment overfishing under existing regulations.

The rFAMS package implements two related measures of spawning potential:

  1. Static SPR (SPR), calculated within the yield-per-recruit (YPR) framework. This metric compares expected lifetime reproductive output under fishing mortality with expected lifetime reproductive output in an unfished population.

  2. Weighted Transitional SPR (wtSPR), calculated within the dynamic pool model. This metric measures annual spawning potential during the transition from one population state to another and accounts for changes in age structure through time.

Static Spawning Potential Ratio

Conceptual Framework

The yield-per-recruit model follows a single recruit throughout its lifetime and estimates cumulative reproductive output under specified mortality schedules. Reproductive output is calculated both with and without fishing mortality. The calculation of SPR requires length at age (derived from the von Bertalanfffy growth model), fecundity at length (based on a linear or logarithmic length-fecundity model), percentage of the proportion that are female, proportion of the females that are spawning, fishing, and natural mortality.

The spawning potential ratio is defined as

SPR=PfishedPunfished SPR=\frac{P_{fished}}{P_{unfished}}

where:

  • PfishedP_{fished} is the total lifetime spawning potential under the specified fishing mortality schedule.
  • PunfishedP_{unfished} is the total lifetime spawning potential in the absence of fishing mortality.

Length-at-Age

Length at age is predicted using the von Bertalanffy Growth Function:

Lt=L∞(1−e−K(t−t0)) L_t=L_{\infty}\left(1-e^{-K(t-t_0)}\right)

where:

  • LtL_t = expected length at age tt
  • L∞L_{\infty} = asymptotic length
  • KK = Brody growth coefficient
  • t0t_0 = theoretical age at which length equals zero

Age-Specific Fecundity

Age-specific fecundity is estimated from fish length using a user-specified fecundity-length relationship. Two model forms are supported.

For a linear relationship:

Fect=β0+β1Lt Fec_t=\beta_0 + \beta_1 L_t

where:

  • FectFec_t = fecundity at age tt
  • LtL_t = mean length at age tt
  • β0\beta_0 = intercept of the fecundity-length relationship
  • β1\beta_1 = slope of the fecundity-length relationship

Alternatively, fecundity can be estimated using a log-transformed relationship.

Fect=exp(β0+β1ln(Lt)) Fec_t=exp(\beta_0 + \beta_1 ln(L_t))

where β0\beta_0 and β1\beta_1 are estimated from the fitted log-linear fecundity model.

Fish younger than the age at maturity are assumed to make no contribution to reproduction. Thus, Fect=0Fec_t = 0 for t<Tmatt<T_{mat}.

Expected reproductive output at age is then adjusted for sex ratio and spawning participation because the total number of individuals in the cohort is constant and not included in the calculation:

Et=Fect×pFt×pSpawnt E_t = Fec_t \times pF_t \times pSpawn_t

where:

  • EtE_t = expected egg production at age tt
  • pFtpF_t = proportion female at age tt
  • pSpawntpSpawn_t = proportion of females that spawn at age tt

Mortality

Total instantaneous mortality at age is

Zt=Ft+Mt Z_t = F_t + M_t

where:

  • FtF_t = instantaneous fishing mortality
  • MtM_t = instantaneous natural mortality

The model allows fishing and natural mortality to vary among length intervals and management regulations.

Survival

Survival over a time interval Δt\Delta t in the absence of fishing is

Snoexp,t=e−MtΔt S_{noexp,t}=e^{-M_t\Delta t}

and survival under fishing is

Sexp,t=e−ZtΔt S_{exp,t}=e^{-Z_t\Delta t}

where Δt\Delta t is the chosen age interval.

Cumulative survival to age tt is

CSnoexp,t=∏i=1tSnoexp,i CS_{noexp,t}=\prod_{i=1}^{t} S_{noexp,i}

for the unfished population and

CSexp,t=∏i=1tSexp,i CS_{exp,t}=\prod_{i=1}^{t} S_{exp,i}

for the fished population.

Spawning Potential

Age-specific spawning potential in the absence of fishing is

Pnoexp,t=Et×CSnoexp,t P_{noexp,t}=E_t \times CS_{noexp,t}

and age-specific spawning potential under fishing is

Pexp,t=Et×CSexp,t P_{exp,t}=E_t \times CS_{exp,t}

Total lifetime spawning potential is obtained by summing across ages:

Punfished=∑tPnoexp,t P_{unfished}=\sum_t P_{noexp,t}

and

Pfished=∑tPexp,t P_{fished}=\sum_t P_{exp,t}

The spawning potential ratio is then

SPR=PfishedPunfished SPR=\frac{P_{fished}}{P_{unfished}}

Values range from 0 to 1.

  • SPR = 1 indicates no reduction in lifetime reproductive output.
  • SPR = 0.40 indicates that reproductive output has been reduced to 40% of unfished levels.
  • SPR approaching 0 indicates severe depletion of spawning capacity.

Weighted Transitional Spawning Potential Ratio

Conceptual Framework

The dynamic pool model explicitly tracks changes in population abundance and age structure through time. Consequently, a single equilibrium SPR is insufficient to describe spawning potential during periods when populations are transitioning toward a new equilibrium.

To characterize reproductive capacity during these transition periods, rFAMS calculates a weighted transitional spawning potential ratio (wtSPR) for each simulation year. This metric compares annual egg production under the simulated fishing regime with the egg production expected if those same fish experienced only natural mortality.

Age-Specific Fecundity

Age-specific fecundity is estimated from fish length using a user-specified fecundity-length relationship in the same manner as with the static SPR. Fish younger than the age at maturity are assumed to have zero fecundity. The resulting age-specific fecundity values are combined with age-specific sex composition, spawning proportion, and survivorship to estimate annual egg production.

Survivorship

Cohort cumulative survivorship under natural mortality is

Snoexp,t=∏i=1te−Mi S_{noexp,t} = \prod_{i=1}^{t} e^{-M_i}

and cumulative survivorship under total mortality is

Sexp,t=∏i=1te−Zi S_{exp,t} = \prod_{i=1}^{t} e^{-Z_i}

where

Zi=Mi+Fi Z_i = M_i + F_i

Egg Production

Expected egg production under natural mortality is

Eggsnoexp,t=N0,t×pFt×pSpawnt×Fect×Snoexp,t Eggs_{noexp,t} = N_{0,t} \times pF_t \times pSpawn_t \times Fec_t \times S_{noexp,t}

Expected egg production under fishing mortality is

Eggsexp,t=N0,t×pFt×pSpawnt×Fect×Sexp,t Eggs_{exp,t} = N_{0,t} \times pF_t \times pSpawn_t \times Fec_t \times S_{exp,t}

where:

  • N0,tN_{0,t} = number of fish entering age class tt
  • FectFec_t = fecundity at age tt
  • pFtpF_t = proportion female at age tt
  • pSpawntpSpawn_t = proportion of females that spawn at age tt
  • Snoexp,tS_{noexp,t} = cumulative survival under natural mortality
  • Sexp,tS_{exp,t} = cumulative survival under total mortality

Annual Weighted Transitional SPR

For each simulation year, egg production is summed across all age classes:

TEnoexp=∑tEggsnoexp,t TE_{noexp} = \sum_t Eggs_{noexp,t}

and

TEexp=∑tEggsexp,t TE_{exp} = \sum_t Eggs_{exp,t}

where:

  • TEnoexpTE_{noexp} = total annual egg production expected under natural mortality only.
  • TEexpTE_{exp} = total annual egg production under the specified fishing regime.

The weighted transitional spawning potential ratio is then

wtSPR=TEexpTEnoexp wtSPR= \frac{TE_{exp}} {TE_{noexp}}

and is calculated separately for every simulated year.

Interpretation

Although both metrics quantify spawning potential relative to an unfished population, they represent different biological perspectives.

Static SPR

Static SPR is an equilibrium measure derived from the yield-per-recruit model. It represents the expected lifetime reproductive contribution of a recruit under a specified mortality schedule and management regulation.

Weighted Transitional SPR

Weighted transitional SPR is an annual population-level measure derived from the dynamic pool model. It reflects realized reproductive output during periods when population age structure is changing following implementation of a management action.

As the population approaches a stable age distribution under constant mortality conditions, wtSPR is expected to converge toward the equilibrium SPR value estimated from the yield-per-recruit model.

Summary

Both SPR metrics quantify the proportion of spawning output retained relative to an unfished population:

SPRorwtSPR=Spawning Output Under FishingSpawning Output Without Fishing SPR \; \text{or} \; wtSPR = \frac{\text{Spawning Output Under Fishing}} {\text{Spawning Output Without Fishing}}

For example, a value of 0.35 indicates that the population is expected to produce 35% of the reproductive output that would occur in the absence of fishing mortality.

Static SPR estimates equilibrium reproductive potential at the recruit level, whereas weighted transitional SPR measures annual population-wide reproductive potential during transitions between population states.

Important note

Both the static and weighted transitional SPR calculated in rFAMS do not match exactly match FAMS. Every effort was made to replicate the output, however, discrepancies between the equations used in FAMS documentation and Parkes (2001) and Goodyear (1993) produced challenges. In addition, the closed source of FAMS prohibits the authors from reviewing the exact methods that were used. We have provided a full description above on how rFAMS calculates SPR and the source code can be viewed on GitHub.
